name: kimss-python-quickstart
description: A 5-minute Python tutorial for the Kimss AI gateway: route OpenAI or Anthropic SDK calls through Kimss so every request is identified, audited, and kill-switchable. Kimss does not host models (BYOI).
general_comments: Public GitHub repo is a force-push mirror of kimssApi/kimss_quickstart/. Prefill for the passing badge only. Silver/gold are out of scope. An authenticated maintainer must still review and save on bestpractices.dev.
description_good_justification: README opening lines state the problem and the one-line fix: track, govern, and secure autonomous agents by pointing the native OpenAI or Anthropic client at the Kimss gateway with an Agent ID header. https://github.com/kimss-ai/kimss-python-quickstart#route-your-first-governed-ai-call-in-5-minutes
interact_justification: Obtain: git clone in README. Feedback: GitHub Issues. Contribute: CONTRIBUTING.md. Security: SECURITY.md. All linked from README.
contribution_justification: https://github.com/kimss-ai/kimss-python-quickstart/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md explains that public main is a force-push mirror, issues are filed on this repo, and code changes land in the monorepo then mirror.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/kimss-ai/kimss-python-quickstart/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#how-changes-land lists acceptable contributions (tutorial accuracy only) and requires python -m unittest discover -s tests.
floss_license_justification: MIT License in LICENSE. SPDX-style badge on the README.
documentation_basics_justification: README and GETTING_STARTED.md cover install, env vars, and running the three example_*.py scripts.
documentation_interface_justification: README documents extra_headers X-Kimss-Agent-Id and X-Kimss-Agent-Name, KIMSS_GATEWAY_URL / KIMSS_WORKSPACE_KEY, and example_03_kill_switch_and_429.py.
sites_https_justification: GitHub repo, kimss.ai, and PyPI links are HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues: https://github.com/kimss-ai/kimss-python-quickstart/issues — searchable, URL-addressable, no proprietary client required.
english_justification: README, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, and source comments are English. Issues are accepted in English.
maintained_justification: The public mirror is updated from the product tree. Recent 2026-08-23 work restored CodeQL, Dependabot, compile CI, CONTRIBUTING.md, and SECURITY.md. Repo created 2026-07-30 and still receiving mirror pushes.
repo_track_justification: git on GitHub records what changed, who, and when.
repo_interim_justification: main is a living tutorial, not a releases-only dump. Git history includes interim mirror commits between any given HEADs.
version_unique_justification: Users clone HEAD of main. Each delivery is uniquely identified by its git commit SHA.
version_semver_justification: This is a continuously mirrored tutorial, not a versioned PyPI package. The kimss SDK on PyPI is a different repo.
version_tags_justification: No GitHub Releases or SemVer tags on this tutorial repo (by design: HEAD is the tutorial).
release_notes_justification: Continuous delivery of a 5-minute tutorial. There are no numbered GitHub Releases of this tree. Users always clone current main rather than upgrading a packaged artifact.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No numbered releases and no publicly known runtime CVEs assigned to this tutorial tree.
report_responses_justification: No public bug reports in the last 2–12 months, so there are none left unacknowledged. We will respond on the GitHub issue tracker.
enhancement_responses_justification: No public enhancement requests in the last 2–12 months. Same tracker as bugs.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: https://github.com/kimss-ai/kimss-python-quickstart/blob/main/SECURITY.md — email security@kimss.ai and GitHub private vulnerability reporting.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledge within 2 business days.
build_justification: Interpreted Python tutorial scripts. Users pip-install requirements and run example_*.py. There is no compiled project artifact to rebuild.
test_justification: FLOSS stdlib suite tests/test_examples_compile.py. Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md. CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml (restored from ci-templates/ci.yml).
test_most_justification: Suite is a syntax/compile check of the tutorial scripts, not branch coverage of a library.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions CI runs unittest discover on every push and pull_request to main.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: changes must keep the examples compiling via python -m unittest discover -s tests.
tests_are_added_justification: When the three example_*.py scripts were established as the tutorial surface, tests/test_examples_compile.py was added and wired into CI.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md Tests section documents the command and that CI runs it on every push.
warnings_justification: CI compiles every example_*.py with py_compile (syntax errors fail the job). CodeQL also runs on push and pull_request.
warnings_fixed_justification: Compile CI fails the push if py_compile raises. We do not merge/mirror tutorial scripts that do not parse.
warnings_strict_justification: No ruff/flake8 gate on this tutorial repo. Passing does not require this SUGGESTED item.
know_secure_design_justification: Primary developers of Kimss work on a production AI gateway (authn, kill switch, audit). At least one primary developer knows the listed secure-design principles (least privilege, complete mediation, fail-safe defaults) as used in the product this tutorial points at.
know_common_errors_justification: Common errors for this kind of client tutorial: leaked API keys, logging secrets, SSRF via attacker-controlled base_url. Mitigations: .env.example with placeholders only, SECURITY.md, no credentials in git, HTTPS only.
crypto_published_justification: Examples do not implement cryptographic protocols. HTTPS is provided by the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs and GitHub.
crypto_keylength_justification: No project-managed keys or configurable key lengths.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Tutorial does not store user passwords.
crypto_random_justification: Tutorial does not generate cryptographic keys or nonces.
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed via git clone over HTTPS from GitHub.
delivery_unsigned_justification: We do not publish an http:// checksum that users are told to trust without a signature. Users clone via HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No medium-or-higher publicly known unpatched vulnerability in this tutorial tree older than 60 days.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No known critical vulnerabilities in this tutorial tree.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: .env.example has placeholders only. .env is not committed. No live private keys in the public tree.
static_analysis_justification: GitHub CodeQL (python, build-mode none) on push, pull_request, and weekly schedule: ci-templates/codeql.yml restored to .github/workflows/codeql.yml.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL includes security-and-quality queries for Python.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No confirmed medium-or-higher exploitable CodeQL findings on the tutorial scripts. Remaining open GitHub code-scanning alerts are OpenSSF Scorecard checks (CII, Maintained, Branch-Protection, etc.), not CodeQL vulns in example_*.py.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL on every push and pull_request to main, plus a weekly cron.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzer or DAST on this 5-minute tutorial. Passing does not require this SUGGESTED item.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic-analysis-discovered exploitable vulnerabilities to fix.
